readings: For each patient sex (SEX from Patient, joined to Examination on ID, so only examinations linked to a patient), compute the average aCL IgG and the average ANA. Each average ignores NULLs in its own column only, so a row with a missing aCL IgG can still count toward the ANA average, and the reverse. Also give each sex's average ANA divided by the mean of the per-sex average ANA values, unrounded.

For each patient sex (SEX from Patient, joined to Examination on ID, so only examinations linked to a patient), compute the average aCL IgG and the average ANA using only examinations where both aCL IgG and ANA are non-NULL, so both averages come from the same set of rows. Also give each sex's average ANA divided by the mean of the per-sex average ANA values (computed on those same rows), unrounded.
queries:
SELECT 
    SEX,
    avg_igg,
    avg_ana,
    avg_ana / (SELECT AVG(avg_ana) FROM (
        SELECT AVG(e.ANA) AS avg_ana
        FROM Patient p
        JOIN Examination e ON p.ID = e.ID
        GROUP BY p.SEX
    )) AS ana_ratio
FROM (
    SELECT p.SEX AS SEX,
           AVG(e.`aCL IgG`) AS avg_igg,
           AVG(e.ANA) AS avg_ana
    FROM Patient p
    JOIN Examination e ON p.ID = e.ID
    GROUP BY p.SEX
);
WITH s AS (
  SELECT P.SEX AS SEX, AVG(E.`aCL IgG`) AS avg_acl_igg, AVG(E.ANA) AS avg_ana
  FROM Examination E
  JOIN Patient P ON P.ID = E.ID
  WHERE E.`aCL IgG` IS NOT NULL AND E.ANA IS NOT NULL
  GROUP BY P.SEX
)
SELECT SEX, avg_acl_igg, avg_ana, avg_ana / (SELECT AVG(avg_ana) FROM s) AS ana_ratio
FROM s;
